what.title: What is a mandalart?
items: Mandal-Art is an idea technique devised in 1987 by Japanese designer Hiroaki Imaizumi. You put a theme in the middle of a 3×3 grid and fill the 8 surrounding cells with whatever comes to mind.
Move each of those 8 cells to the center of its own block and the grid grows to 9×9, 81 cells: 1 core goal, 8 sub-goals and 64 actions, which is why it's popular as a goal planner.

It became widely known through the goal sheet baseball player Shohei Ohtani wrote in his first year of high school. His core goal was 'first-round pick by 8 teams', and his 8 sub-goals were body building, control, pitch sharpness, 160 km/h speed, breaking balls, luck, character and mental strength.
The point is breaking a big goal down to actions you can take today. The fixed number of cells makes you think about every side, not just one.

howTo.title: How to fill it in
items: Open the center block and write your core goal in the very middle. A deadline or number, like 'this year' or '5 kg', helps.
Write the 8 things you need to reach that goal in the surrounding cells. Include foundations like health, mindset and relationships, not just skills.
Each sub-goal is copied to the middle of its outer block automatically. Open the blocks one by one and fill in 8 actions.
You don't have to fill all 64 cells at once. Write what comes to mind first and fill the gaps over the next few days.
When you're done, save it as an image or print it on A4 landscape and put it where you'll see it.

actions.title: Writing good actions
items: Start with a verb. Instead of 'health', write 'walk 8,000 steps a day' so the action is clear.
Add a number so it's measurable. A count, time or amount makes it obvious whether you did it.
Make it small enough to do today or this week. If it's too big, that cell becomes another goal.
Only write actions you control. 'Pass the exam' is a result; 'do 5 years of past exams 3 times' is an action.
Mixing daily habits and one-off tasks is fine. Check habits often and check one-off tasks once they're finished.

tips.title: Tips for this tool
items: On a phone, use 'Edit a block' to write one block at a time in large cells, and 'Full chart' to see all 81 cells at once.
Your entries and checks are saved in this browser automatically. Come back in January, tap 'Done' on what you did and see your progress.
Send the share link and the other person sees the same chart. Their own chart stays untouched until they press 'Save as my chart'.
To continue on another device, copy the link and open it there. If that device has no saved chart, it becomes your chart right away; if it already has one, press 'Save as my chart' to replace it.

items.q: How do I fill in a mandalart template?
items.a: Write the core goal in the center cell, 8 sub-goals in the cells around it, and 8 actions for each sub-goal in its outer block. In this tool you write each sub-goal once and it appears in the middle of its outer block automatically.

items.q: Do I have to fill all 64 cells?
items.a: No. Writing actions you'll actually take matters more than filling every cell. You can save, print and share with empty cells, and progress counts only the action cells you filled.

items.q: Are a mandalart and a mandala chart the same thing?
items.a: Both are the same 3×3 grid expanded to 9×9. Mandal-Art is the name used by designer Hiroaki Imaizumi (1987), and Mandala Chart by management consultant Yasuo Matsumura (1979). Shohei Ohtani's goal sheet is described as based on the Mandala Chart.

items.q: What was on Shohei Ohtani's mandalart?
items.a: He made it in his first year at Hanamaki Higashi High School. The core goal was 'first-round pick by 8 teams', and the 8 sub-goals were body building, control, pitch sharpness, 160 km/h speed, breaking balls, luck, character and mental strength.
Only in the browser you're using (localStorage); nothing is sent to a server. It won't appear if you clear browser data or open another device, so keep a link or image as well.

items.q: Does the share link include my 'Done' checks?
items.a: No. The link holds only the chart text, compressed. Checks are your personal progress, so they stay in this browser.

items.q: How do I print or save an image?
items.a: Press 'Save chart image' to download the 9×9 chart as mandalart.png. 'Print' fits it on one A4 landscape page, and you can save it as a PDF from the print dialog.
